Checkpoint 2 • 7 minutes

Choose the channel

A sensible message can still cause a problem if it reaches the wrong audience or clutters the wrong place.

Where should it go?

Decide
EmailFormal, detailed or includes a file.
Class commentVisible to everyone on that post.
Private commentAbout your own assignment.
Do not sendSensitive, unsafe or unnecessary.

Audience check

Before posting, ask:

1
Who needs this?One person, the teacher or the whole class?
2
Does it belong here?Keep assignment questions with the assignment.
3
Would I say this in class?A digital record can be copied or revisited.

Class comments are not a group chat

Post only when the teacher invites responses or your message genuinely helps the learning. A private question about your work belongs in a private comment. Personal or sensitive information does not belong in either.

Checkpoint 2 ready?Six channels chosen correctly and one reason explained.
Checkpoint 3 • 8 minutes

Message makeover

Professional does not mean long or unnatural. It means the reader can understand the purpose and act without chasing missing detail.

The rushed version

Needs a reroute
SubjectHELP!!!
hi sir i wasnt in what did i miss send it pls
Think: What would the reader still need to ask? Which part sounds demanding rather than useful?

Build the message route

Repair

Move the six parts into the order a reader should meet them.

Move the parts, then check your route.

Rewrite it

Include a greeting, purpose, useful detail, polite request and your name.

Pre-send check

Email creates a record.Write as if the message may be read again later.
Checkpoint 3 ready?Order correct, email rewritten and three checks confirmed.
Checkpoint 4 • 7 minutes

Email controls

Every control changes who receives the message or what travels with it. Use each one for a reason.

Quick control guide

TOMain recipient. This person is expected to read or act.
CCKeeps someone informed. Their address is visible.
BCCHides recipients from one another. Use only when appropriate.
↩ REPLYAnswers the sender. Usually the safest response.
↩ ALLAnswers everyone. Use only if everyone needs it.
📎 + ⚑Attachment sends a file. Flag marks a message for attention.

Choose the precise control

Choose

Reply all test

Do all recipients need my answer? If the answer is no, do not use Reply all.

Flags help organise messages. They do not make every message urgent.

Checkpoint 4 ready?Six controls correct and Reply all explained.
Checkpoint 5 • 9 minutes

Download without drama

A download is useful only when the source is expected, the file makes sense and you can find it again.

Safe, check or stop?

Judge

Decide whether each download is ready, needs checking, or should be stopped.

Your controlled download

1Use the teacher file in Classroom, or the practice button below.
2Choose the correct ICT folder, not a mystery Downloads pile.
3Rename it with your first name and keep .txt.
4Open it and check it is the file you expected.

The practice file is a small text document created by this workbook.

My Documents→Year 8→ICT - TGCh→Firstname_Departure_Briefing.txt

Checkpoint 6 • 9 minutes

Collaborate without chaos

Collaboration means improving shared work while protecting everyone else’s contribution.

Four rules at the collaboration gate

READRead the assignment and the existing ideas first.
PLACEWork only in your assigned slide, row or section.
ADDContribute something specific rather than repeating.
CHECKReview your change and leave other work intact.

Classroom control

Apply

Shared-work sequence

Move the steps into a safe and useful order.

Move the steps, then check the sequence.

Your contribution

Open the shared item in the Departure 02 assignment. Use the space your teacher gives you.

Specific feedback: name what works, explain why, then suggest one achievable next step. “Good work” is kind, but it does not help someone improve.

Evidence and checks

Add collaboration evidenceShow your contribution and useful response, not the whole class list.
Checkpoint 6 ready?Controls and sequence correct, contribution written, checks and evidence complete.
Checkpoint 7 • 11 minutes

Send-ready mission

Bring the routines together in one professional email with the file you downloaded. Prepare it carefully, then send only when your teacher gives the signal.

Your live mission

Open school email, start a new message and use the address book to select your ICT teacher.
Use the subject Departure 02 | Your name | Your form.
Write a greeting, one useful routine you learned, a polite closing and your name.
Attach Firstname_Departure_Briefing.txt, then open the attachment chip to check it.
Proofread, wait for the teacher’s signal, send, then check the message in Sent Items.
CC is not automatic. Use it only if your teacher assigns an approved partner. Never guess an address.
